newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya air traffic go-slow enters sixth day.
newsitem.headline: Kenya air traffic go-slow enters sixth day.

text.p: Air traffic delays continued for a sixth day in Kenya on Thursday despite the use of senior aviation officials to ease a go-slow by air traffic controllers, aviation and government sources said.

"The government has brought in instructors and other senior industry people normally not in these stations. So, at least for Nairobi, delays are shorter now," said a senior industry official. "Mombasa is still pretty bad."
Air traffic controllers are demanding a 50-fold increase from what they say is pay of about $90 a month, plus benefits.
Labour Minister Philip Masinde scheduled a news conference for 11 a.m. (0800 GMT) to make a formal government statement on the glo-slow.
On Tuesday Masinde ordered the controllers to open negotiations and resume work but the order was ignored.
Foreign airlines and freight forwarders said they were increasingly concerned about safety at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport.
"We are very concerned about air safety," said Olav Everts, regional manager for Royal Dutch Airlines KLM.

"Air safety is a serious concern, you have too many flights around here, aeroplanes just flying around waiting to land. That creates a very big danger for an accident," added one official with a European freight forwarder.
Everts said KLM had expressed concerns over the continuing delays at the airports to the aviation authorities who he said had been "unapproachable" when contacted by KLM.
At least 40 airlines use Kenyan airports and landing and parking fees brings millions of dollars in revenue.
On Wednesday, a Dutch-owned freight forwarder Flower Wing said it had lost some $50,000 in a cargo shipment of flowers due to the go-slow.
"This is really getting bad. We had three chartered flights out of here Monday, all with fresh produce, which were all delayed, one ... for 18 hours," said a Flower Wing official.

He said the three chartered flights -- with MartinAir, Cargolux and Uganda's DasAir -- were destined for Amsterdam. Most of the cargo was flowers for the auctions in the Netherlands, which they had missed.

"The delays are bad for the flowers, bad for the avocados. We are losing money like mad. We had to throw half a load of flowers away, almost 10 tonnes. You are talking about over $50,000 just for that shipment," the official told Reuters.
Airports at Nairobi, the coast city of Mombasa, Kisumu and the tourist resort of Malindi were hit hard by the dispute.
Gulf Air was forced to cancel its weekly flight to Uganda via Nairobi from Muscat. A Gulf Air official said it would fly only to Nairobi and back to Muscat until further notice.

Lufthansa Cargo said it was considering cancelling a Boeing 747 from Nairobi on Friday amid "serious concerns" over air safety because of the go-slow and a general strike called for Friday by an opposition-backed alliance.
David Keary, general manager for East and Central Africa for Lufthansa Cargo, said he estimated total losses from the cargo load scheduled for Friday to be worth about $400,000.

Freddy Ganz, Jomo Kenyatta International Airport station manager for Swissair, Royal Dutch Airlines KLM and Sabena, told Reuters his flights were "heavily delayed" -- normally one hour on arrival and departure.
The go-slow increased pressure on a government hit by the International Monetary Fund's decision last week to halt a $205 million aid package,citing concern at high-level corruption.
He declined to give any details of the agreement to end the go-slow, which had entered a sixth day earlier on Thursday.

But air controllers told Reuters they returned to normal work after being assured that a report presented to President Daniel arap Moi on Wednesday on the terms and conditions of service for government workers would meet their concerns.
Air traffic controllers had demanded a 50-fold increase from what they say is pay of about $90 a month, plus benefits.
On Tuesday, Masinde had ordered the controllers to open negotiations and resume work but the order was ignored.
